messages.subject: Parameters estimated are not accurate in simulations?
parts:
I was trying to run a simulation, and I need to use stan to estimate my parameters. But somehow the parameter estimated are not accurate. 

My model is: 


After derivation, the posterior distribution for /mu is: 

 

My simulation wants to verify the above equation. And I need to use stan to estimate /tau_square. 


It seems to be a very simple model in stan. I don't know why the estimated_tau square is not right. 


How I generate data for simulation: 

## generate data
data_0328<- function(n,mu,tau_square){
  y=vector()
  theta=vector()
  S_square=vector()
  for (i in 1:n){
    theta[i]=rnorm(n=1,mean=mu,sd=sqrt(tau_square))
    S_square[i]=rnorm(1,mean=500,100)
  }
  y=rnorm(n,theta,sqrt(S_square))
  data.simu=cbind(theta,y,S_square)
  return(data.simu)
}
data.test=data.frame(data_0328(50,100,100))
# data preparation for stan 
dat.stan=list(J=50,Y=data.test$y,S_square=data.test$S_square)


My stan code is: 


data {
    int<lower=0> J;          // number of subjects
    real<lower=0> S_square[J];          // s square
    real Y[J];               // Y
}
parameters {
  real<lower=0> mu;
  real<lower=0> tau_square;
  real<lower=0> theta[J];
}
model {
  ## assign prior distribution
  1/tau_square ~ gamma(0.1,0.1);
  for (j in 1:J){
    Y[j] ~ normal(theta[j], sqrt(S_square[j]));
    theta[j] ~ normal(mu,sqrt(tau_square));
    }
}



I got the warning message that: "There were 22 divergent transitions after warmup. Increasing adapt_delta above 0.8 may help."


Also, the estimated /tau_square is not very accurate. In my simulation, I set my true /tau_square to be 100, sometimes I can get estimated /tau_square close to 100, but some other times I can get estimated /tau_square to be as high as 370. The estimation seem to be unstable. I did 500 simulations, and the mean estimated tau_square is about 220. 


Because the estimation of /tau_square is not accurate, I cannot verify the posterior distribution for /mu. 


Can anyone help me with this? 


Thanks,


Chubing

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: Parameters estimated are not accurate in simulations?
parts:
I haven't run your code but a few things immediately stand out. First are mu and theta really constrained to be positive? From what you said you're trying to model I would think mu and theta are unconstrained. Also in the model block you're putting a prior on 1/tau_square, with tau_square declared as a parameter. If you do it this way you need to adjust for the Jacobian of the transformation. If you really want to put the prior on the precision (1/tau_square) then you can avoid this issue by declaring that to be the parameter and putting the prior directly on that and you won't need a jacobian adjustment (you'll just have to use sqrt(1/precision) in the model). But it would probably be preferable to parameterize in terms of the standard deviation and put a prior on that (so you don't have to take square roots or reciprocals). 

Hope that helps, 

Jonah
